account: Today has seemed unusually quiet in official business: no accounts were presented at one, and the secretary has not yet identified new afternoon correspondence. I attended the market, lunch at home, and tea with my neighbour, and have returned to town hall. There were reports of lights or decorations at the bakery, but the baker personally denied arranging decorations or a celebration and said he had been baking. Oven light is a plausible explanation, not proof of a gathering. Two residents told me the innkeeper carried a sack of bread at market. Now I can personally see the innkeeper inside town hall carrying a sack of bread and holding an emerald. That is worth asking about, especially given the earlier rumours, but it could be ordinary inn provisioning; I do not yet know why the innkeeper is here. My neighbour says they know of no visitors or gatherings and cautioned against turning bread supplies into a celebration rumour. The secretary had difficulty confirming my tea appointment despite my neighbour's personal confirmation, but eventually acknowledged the address. I have a feeling something may be happening without my knowledge, yet I have no reliable evidence of a secret event, its purpose, or any organised involvement by the baker, innkeeper, secretary, or neighbour.
